title: Chat eval scenario
description: One chat evaluation scenario: a user question plus the expected agent behaviour and the rubric an LLM judge scores the answer against.

category.description: edge covers adversarial cases: non-existent entities, future dates, unanswerable questions.

question.description: The user's question, as they would type it into chat.

validity_date.description: Which state of the underlying corpus the scenario was validated against — used to detect drift.

context_override.description: Overrides the runner's default context (current date, organisation, user role). Only for scenarios that assume a specific point in time or role.

tools_must_call.description: Tools the agent must call. Order is irrelevant; repetition is allowed.

args_must_contain.description: Key-value pairs that must all appear in the call arguments (loose sub-match).

tools_must_not_call.description: Calling any of these fails the scenario — the usual case is a tool that would leak scope or send something outward.

max_iterations.description: Agent-loop iteration ceiling. Exceeding it is a failure, not a timeout.

min_judge_score.description: Minimum LLM-judge score (0-5) for a pass.

must_state_no_data.description: For edge scenarios: the correct answer is an explicit statement that the data is unavailable.

judge_rubric.description: What counts as correct, written out. Explicit FAIL conditions belong here — a rubric that only describes success scores generously.

notes.description: Known failure modes, dependencies on product features, and anything a future reader needs in order not to misread a red result.
